summary.headline: Bharat Forge Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose about 30% YoY to INR2,526 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25.9%.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly export and domestic sales, with standalone revenue of INR2,526 crore (up almost 30% YoY) and EBITDA of INR655 crore (up 20%, 25.9% margin). Consolidated revenue was INR4,870 crore (up 21%) with EBITDA of INR778 crore (up about 9%, around 16% margin). Freight, energy and input cost inflation compressed margins, with pass-through to customers lagging; management flagged an optical impact of about 0.4% on margins. Defence order book stood at INR10,950 crore as of September, and the ATAGS bulk production clearance has been received, with revenue recognition expected from Q1 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: legal and consultancy charges for Europe steel restructuring

financial_highlights.value: INR476 crore / about INR6.7 crore negative

segments.name: Standalone / export CV and automotive
segments.commentary: Export CV business recorded its highest revenue, driven by volume growth, market share gains and ramp-up of new businesses. Standalone revenue grew almost 30% YoY.

segments.name: JS Auto Cast and K-Drive (India acquisitions)
segments.commentary: JS Auto Cast revenue INR220 crore (up 16%) with record quarterly EBITDA up 35%. Combined JSA and K-Drive quarterly run rate is about INR600 crore, up from about INR400 crore at acquisition for JSA and about INR300 crore for K-Drive, with FY27 combined revenue guided above INR2,200-2,300 crore.

segments.name: Europe (steel restructuring)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR931 crore and EBITDA INR29 crore (about 3.1% margin), despite lower utilisation from holidays and a difficult operating environment. Restructuring expected to conclude by mid-next year.

segments.name: US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue INR476 crore with EBITDA about INR6.7 crore negative. Steel subsidiary hit by one-time breakdowns; aluminium subsidiary faces raw material cost issues.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with recovery of price and cost increases from customers and ramp-up of new businesses.
Management expects 20%-25% revenue growth guidance to be met, driven across aerospace, industrial exports, semiconductor, CV, passenger car exports, marine, JSA and K-Drive.
Excluding 2%-3% inflationary impact on top line, H2 EBITDA growth expected to be in line with or slightly better than top-line growth.
India manufacturing: expected to exceed INR5,000 crore quarterly sales by end of next year (from about INR3,000-3,400 crore per quarter at 22% margin), with at least 200-250 bps margin accretion.
Defence margins expected at 20%-24/25% depending on mix; ATAGS starts around 20%-21% and could rise 200-300 bps with fully filled ammunition.
K-Drive target: double-digit EBITDA margin within 2 years and revenue growth of at least 20%-25% a year.
US steel subsidiary solution targeted by December; US aluminium subsidiary expected to turn above break-even within 6-12 months as new non-auto products ramp.
Europe restructuring (CDP) to conclude by mid-next year.
capex_capacity: Baramati brownfield expansion of about INR1,300 crore across forging and machining, adding about 100,000 tonnes of forging capacity and a large machining facility; expected to more than double Baramati output over 2-3 years.
Production trials for first two Baramati assets from January-March 2027, third asset mid-2027, last asset end-2027.
New aerospace-dedicated manufacturing facility starting mid-next year, about 60% already sold out.
New forging facility for aerospace, semiconductor and industrial high-value large parts to lift semiconductor business 2-3x; current run rate is double-digit USD million per year.
Current non-automotive capacity running very close to full for the last few quarters.
demand_pricing: Aerospace: significant new engine and landing gear business won, described as double-digit USD million per year over long period (about USD100-120 million lifecycle); customer not named.
Semiconductor: new business described as large double-digit USD million per year, with full machining planned to add value.
Class 8 truck (US) and India: customers are seeking to block capacity for 18-20 months; production expected stable to slightly stronger, per Subodh Tandale.
Steel cost in India follows global price trends; Indian safeguard-duty-inflated costs are not passed through to customers.
Defence order inflow of INR2,100 crore across India manufacturing in H1, including INR1,000 crore in Forgings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new aerospace order the Pratt & Whitney contract for mission-critical engine components?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not name the customer; said it has won significant new business from multiple customers and products, and a new aerospace-dedicated facility is about 60% sold out.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of H2 revenue jump to meet 20%-25% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Broad-based: aerospace, industrial exports, semicon, CV, passenger car exports, marine, JSA and K-Drive, with many new programmes moving into revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATAGS timing and how long to deliver?
qa_highlights.answer: Order not deferred; production approval was delayed. Revenue from Q1 FY28; 184 guns to be delivered over about 4 years with ramp-up, and revenue split roughly 10%, 15%, 20% then remainder by year.

qa_highlights.question: How will CQB contract timing work?
qa_highlights.answer: CQB bulk production clearance not yet received; delivery expected to start 4-6 months after clearance. Capacity estimated at 120-150 guns a year.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin for India manufacturing and K-Drive profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: India manufacturing margin expected to add 200-250 bps; K-Drive targets double-digit EBITDA margin within 2 years with 20-25% annual growth, expanding into passenger car, SUV, pickup and utility segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving US subsidiary losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel subsidiary had one-time breakdowns, with a fix targeted by December; aluminium subsidiary has raw material cost issues and new non-auto products expected to lift profitability in 6-12 months.

risks_watch: Pass-through lag on freight, energy and raw material inflation, with about 2%-3% top-line inflationary impact in H2.
ATAGS revenue depends on customer absorption and induction schedule; CQB bulk production clearance pending.
US steel subsidiary breakdowns and aluminium raw material costs; profitability target depends on fixes by December and new product ramp.
Europe steel restructuring (CDP) execution through mid-next year with legal and consultancy exceptional charges.
Execution of Baramati capacity ramp and aerospace/semiconductor facility commissioning timelines.
Management did not name the aerospace customer; disclosure of order details remains limited.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on order wins, capacity expansion and H2 recovery, with specific numerical targets. Less specific on customer names and ATAGS revenue phasing, and somewhat defensive on US subsidiary losses and the order-book/deferral question.
key_quotes: So, with a strong balance sheet, lots of new orders, now execution will deliver stronger return in the next 6 months and going forward.
I would expect second half to be stronger than first half.
The order has not been deferred, the production approval didn't get deferred, it got delayed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides at least 200-250 bps margin accretion in India manufacturing (currently ~22% margin) by end of next year, plus H2 EBITDA growth in line with or slightly above revenue growth after price and cost recovery; offset by 2-3% inflation drag and Europe margin ~3.1%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Baramati INR1,300 crore expansion (~100,000 t forging) is under implementation with trials Jan-Mar 2027, third asset mid-2027, last end-2027; new aerospace facility starts mid-next year (~60% sold out).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance for 20-25% revenue growth is expected to be met (midpoint 22.5%), with H2 stronger than H1 across aerospace, CV, marine, semicon and JSA/K-Drive, supported by a INR10,950 crore defence order book and non-auto capacity running near full.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation has been very close to full for several quarters and non-auto capacity is near full, with the INR1,300 crore Baramati and new aerospace/semicon forging plans already in progress, so further capex announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident in meeting 20-25% revenue growth and H2 recovery, but the 2-3% inflation drag and ATAGS/CQB clearance timing cap any upgrade case.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight, energy and raw material pass-through lags with a 2-3% top-line inflation impact; US steel breakdowns need a December fix and ATAGS revenue starts only from Q1 FY28, all of which could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New aerospace engine and landing gear business (double-digit USD million per year), semiconductor machining, and K-Drive passenger car/SUV/pickup segments are ramping into revenue; the aerospace facility starts mid-next year.

rows.label: ATAGS revenue from Q1 FY28
rows.why: Bulk production clearance received with revenue recognition expected from Q1 FY28; 184 guns over about 4 years, ramp split roughly 10%, 15%, 20% then remainder.

rows.label: US steel subsidiary fix and aluminium break-even
rows.why: Steel subsidiary solution targeted by December after one-time breakdowns, and aluminium expected above break-even within 6-12 months, but US EBITDA was about INR6.7 crore negative on INR476 crore revenue.

rows.label: Europe steel restructuring (CDP) completion
rows.why: Europe revenue INR931 crore with EBITDA INR29 crore (~3.1% margin); restructuring to conclude by mid-next year with exceptional charges (about INR20 crore in Q2).

tone.note: Management was confident on the 20-25% growth guide, Baramati capacity, defence order book and India manufacturing margin accretion, but cautious on freight/energy pass-through, US subsidiary losses and ATAGS phasing; analysts pressed on the unnamed aerospace customer and the order-book deferral que
